title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - MedTech Systems
next_steps: Redwood to send Private Networking checklist and SOC2 & KMS docs
Schedule perf benchmark (end-to-end) for sample workload next Tuesday
Customer to provision VPC peering / PrivateLink and share CIDR & account IDs
Agree final POC success criteria and timeline (target sign-off by end of POC)
action_items: Alex Kim (Redwood AE): Share private-networking checklist + security pack (due 2025-06-18)
Jordan Lee (Redwood SE): Prepare benchmark harness + perf test script (due 2025-06-20)
Mark Dunn (MedTech): Provide VPC CIDR, AWS account ID, and list of allowed egress ranges (due 2025-06-17)
Lena Ortiz (MedTech): Confirm encryption/KMS provider requirements and compliance questions (due 2025-06-19)
summary: POC scoping for a 4-week private networking POC focused on data residency and egress constraints. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink, regional requirements (us-east-1 + eu-west-1), success criteria (latency P95, throughput and quality checks), benchmark plan, and timeline/owners.
topics: POC success criteria and SLA targets
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-15 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~53m | Attendees: Alex, Jordan, Sofia (Redwood); Priya, Mark, Lena, Tom (MedTech)

Summary: quick intro, confirm scope = private networking + data residency + run perf benchmarks; agree POC timeline = 4 weeks.

[00:00] Alex Kim (AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round of intros?
[00:18] Priya Shah (VP Eng): hi all, priya here — vp eng at medtech systems, i own integrations and infra decisions.
[00:25] Mark Dunn (Infra): mark, infra lead. we'll handle network setup and security approvals.
[00:30] Jordan Lee (SE): jordan from redwood, i'll run the perf tests and help with the private deployment side.
[00:38] Lena Ortiz (Security): lena, security architect — primarily around KMS, egress controls, compliance.
[00:45] Alex Kim (AE): cool. goal today: scope a POC for private networking and residency. get to success criteria, required benchmarks, and a timeline.

[01:12] Alex Kim (AE): priya, can you recap the must-haves from your side — what would make this POC a success?
[01:28] Priya Shah (VP Eng): yeah, we have three main things: one, data must not leave the region, so we need region pinning and residency in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for different customers. two, latency — our user workflows are sensitive, we want P95 under ~300ms for generation calls in the common path. three, security — SOC2-level auditability, KMS integration and no public egress except to audited endpoints.
[01:56] Alex Kim (AE): great, that's helpful. jordan — from an engineering side, can we meet those?
[02:05] Jordan Lee (SE): yes. we have two deployment options here: hosted with VPC peering to your VPC or a PrivateLink/Interface endpoint setup. both can keep traffic inside your network and control egress. VPC peering is simpler but has cross-account routing limits; PrivateLink gives endpoint-level control and avoids route table changes, but needs extra endpoint configuration.
[02:38] Tom Baker (ML Eng): any differences for performance? PrivateLink adds an extra hop, does it add meaningful latency?
[02:48] Jordan Lee (SE): small, typically 5-15ms depending on region and AZ path; in our experience it's within P95 budgets but we should benchmark. peering often has slightly lower added latency but is more brittle for large multi-account orgs.

[03:25] Mark Dunn (Infra): we also have strict egress; the network team won't allow arbitrary outbound to public IPs. can you support egress-restricted deployments where only specific hostnames/cidrs are allowed?
[03:40] Jordan Lee (SE): yes — we can publish a set of egress IPs and domains for the POC; or ideally, we run inside your VPC with no public egress, leveraging PrivateLink. we also support NAT with restricted routes. note: some of our telemetry/metrics ingestion needs outbound to your monitoring endpoints — that can be routed to endpoints you control.

[04:15] Lena Ortiz (Security): on KMS — we require CMEK/HSM for key control. can redwood support customer-managed keys and integrate with our AWS KMS?
[04:25] Alex Kim (AE): short answer: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in Private deployments. jordan, can you confirm the specifics?
[04:33] Jordan Lee (SE): yes — for Private we support bringing your own KMS key; we can encrypt data at rest with your key and provide audit logs. for hosted+peering we can do envelope encryption with your key in some configurations; i'll add details to the security pack.

[05:02] Priya Shah (VP Eng): about regions — we have eu customers too. do you have deployments in eu-west-1?
[05:10] Jordan Lee (SE): we have capacity in eu-west-1; for the POC we can spin up a dedicated stack in that region. one ask: we need approx sizing info — concurrency and tokens per second — to size the instance footprints.
[05:30] Tom Baker (ML Eng): typical workload: ~10 qps of generation calls, ~600 tokens per call average (medical summaries), peak concurrency of 40. so overall tokens/sec in peak ~ 40 * (600 / 1s?) — erm, that's odd — let me rephrase: request rate 10 rps steady, burst to 40 concurrent, average generation latency ~1s currently. total token throughput about 6k tokens/sec at peak.
[06:05] Jordan Lee (SE): good. for that workload we recommend a dedciated node pool with 4 x A100-ish GPUs or equivalent depending on model quantization. for hosted POC smaller GPUs with batching might suffice. we'll run quantized model profiles and give you recommended capacity after initial bench.
[06:28] Mark Dunn (Infra): can you run the benchmark harness inside our VPC? we prefer the traffic never leave.
[06:34] Jordan Lee (SE): yes — we can deploy the benchmark agent in your VPC and execute load tests against the private endpoint. requires an endpoint (PrivateLink) or peering and subnets for the test runner.

[07:05] Alex Kim (AE): timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) — exchange network details, security questionnaire; week 1 — provision endpoints and initial small-scale perf runs; week 2 — full benchmark across peak workload and stress tests; week 3 — quality checks, evals with your prompt sets and finalize success criteria; week 4 — review and decision. thoughts?
[07:30] Priya Shah (VP Eng): sounds reasonable but we need procurement and legal sign-off to access certain infra; can we start network prep in parallel so we don't block?
[07:42] Alex Kim (AE): yes, parallelize. we'll send security docs and a checklist so your legal/security can review without infra access.

[08:10] Lena Ortiz (Security): please include our questions: data retention policy, deletion workflows, access controls, RBAC, audit log formats, and whether any PHI flows through telemetry.
[08:25] Sofia Alvarez (CSM): we'll include a data flow diagram and redact telemetry to avoid PHI collection; note in the POC we can switch telemetry to aggregated only.

[09:00] Tom Baker (ML Eng): back to benchmarks — can we run both latency P95 and sample-throughput with KV cache warm/cold? we want to see cold-starts for new sessions and warmed flows for recurrent prompts.
[09:15] Jordan Lee (SE): yes — benchmark harness supports warm vs cold cache runs, variable context lengths, and simulated multi-tenant traffic. we'll share the harness config and a spreadsheet for recording results.
[09:35] Alex Kim (AE): success criteria recap (Priya, confirm): 1) Data residency enforced per region, 2) Latency P95 < 300ms for typical generation path, 3) Throughput to support 40 concurrent at acceptable cost, 4) Security controls meet SOC2/KMS expectations, 5) Zero unauthorized egress.
[10:02] Priya Shah (VP Eng): yes, that's the set. add an item: quality checks — model outputs must meet existing accuracy thresholds on our eval set (we'll share prompts + expected labels).
[10:14] Jordan Lee (SE): we'll run automated evals and report regressions; we can also pin to model versions if that helps.

[11:00] Mark Dunn (Infra): one concern: privateLink pricing and cross-AZ throughput limits; any advice to avoid throttles?
[11:10] Jordan Lee (SE): PrivateLink can have ENI limits per AZ — for production we'd typically provision multiple endpoints across AZs and use cross-AZ routing. for POC a single endpoint per AZ is fine; we'll provide recommended endpoint counts. also can test with path MTU considerations.

[12:00] Priya Shah (VP Eng): are there any ports/protocols required outbound from our side for, say, metrics ingestion?
[12:08] Jordan Lee (SE): mostly HTTPS to specific domains/IPs; we'll provide exact hostnames and IP ranges. if you host metrics internally we can post to your endpoint over HTTPS.

[13:00] Alex Kim (AE): procurement question — do we need a formal SOW before we start the POC?
[13:07] Priya Shah (VP Eng): legal prefers a short mutual NDA and a statement of work for the POC to define responsibilities.
[13:15] Alex Kim (AE): we can do a standard POC SOW template; i'll share that along with pricing for dedicated POC capacity.

[14:00] Tom Baker (ML Eng): regarding model selection — we plan to evaluate a 7B quantized model and a 13B variant for quality tradeoffs. will you support both?
[14:10] Jordan Lee (SE): yes. we'll provide both model variants and run A/B in the POC. note: quantization profiles differ by model — we'll recommend kernels and batch sizes.

[15:00] Lena Ortiz (Security): side question — audit logs retention and who has access? we need logs retained 1 year and integration with our SIEM.
[15:12] Jordan Lee (SE): we can export audit logs to your S3 with lifecycle policy or push to your SIEM. retention policy configurable; we'll outline options in the security pack.

[16:00] Alex Kim (AE): ok, let's align on concrete bench metrics we'll measure: P95 latency, P99 latency, avg tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens estimate, failed requests %, and model quality regression on your eval set. anyone add?
[16:20] Priya Shah (VP Eng): also measure cold-start latency for new sessions and impact of KV cache misses.
[16:30] Jordan Lee (SE): got it. we'll include warm/cold runs and single-request as well as multi-request per session tests.

[18:00] Mark Dunn (Infra): network details I'll send: VPC CIDR x.x.x.x/16, account ID 123456789012, and a list of subnets for endpoints. expect that by EOD tomorrow.
[18:10] Alex Kim (AE): perfect. once we have that, jordan will give the exact IAM policy and endpoint config.

[19:00] Jordan Lee (SE): for the benchmark harness — we'll need a small runner instance in your VPC (t3.medium or similar) and permissions to call the endpoint. also we'll provide a docker image to run locally if you prefer.

[20:00] Priya Shah (VP Eng): about POC length — if all goes well can we aim to finish within 3 weeks? maybe compress week 2+3.
[20:10] Alex Kim (AE): possible, depends on procurement and network setup speed. let's keep 4 weeks as target but try to accelerate.

[22:00] Sofia Alvarez (CSM): i'll coordinate scheduling and the security pack; alex i'll follow up with slides and the SOW template.

[23:00] Discussion: brief back-and-forth clarifying egress hostnames, KMS flow, and PrivateLink endpoint count. small crosstalk; some words mis-transcribed ("Private Link" vs "PrivateLink").

[30:00] Jordan Lee (SE): quick note on cost: during POC we'll provide a cost estimate; dedicated nodes cost depends on GPU class and utilization — we'll provide a sheet with expected cost per 1k tokens for both quantized and full precision.

[36:00] Tom Baker (ML Eng): for quality checks — we'll send a 200-prompt eval set, and expect you to run candidate outputs through our scoring script.

[36:15] Jordan Lee (SE): yes, please send the eval set and scoring script; we'll run it as part of the POC and include result CSV.

[40:00] Alex Kim (AE): any blockers left?
[40:08] Priya Shah (VP Eng): main blocker is legal sign-off for the POC SOW and our security team review time. if those take longer than a week, timeline slips.

[40:20] Alex Kim (AE): understood. we'll provide materials to accelerate review.

[45:00] Quick recap of next steps: redwood sends security pack, SOW, and benchmark harness; medtech to provide VPC details and procurement timeline; schedule perf run for next Tue slot.

[46:30] Priya Shah (VP Eng): agreed. please also include a short diagram of data flows for our security review.

[46:40] Sofia Alvarez (CSM): will do.

[50:00] Closing: thanks all. Alex confirm you'll share action list?

[50:06] Alex Kim (AE): yes — i'll email the checklist, the SOW draft, and set up the perf slot. thanks everyone.

[52:00] Call ends.
